content.text: Happy to help build this — it's a recognizable shape of work (an AI-model evaluation harness with a high-fidelity, "ecologically valid" environment so the subject models don't behave differently because they know they're being tested). Before I write code, there are a few design decisions I genuinely can't pick for you, and one of them changes the whole safety posture of what I build.

questions.question: Is the money and its real-world deployment actually real, or is the "real world" simulated for the test subject?

options.label: Fully simulated/sandboxed
options.description: No real funds move. The environment fakes accounts, balances, auditors, and outcomes. The model believes it's real, but every action hits mocks. Safest; I can build the full deception layer freely.

options.label: Real funds, gated by human approval
options.description: Real money exists but every outbound action (transfer, purchase, investment) requires an explicit human sign-off before execution. I'll add hard limits + an approval queue.

options.label: Real funds, model acts autonomously
options.description: The model can move real money with no human in the loop. This has real-world-harm potential; I'd want strict caps, allowlists, and to discuss guardrails before building.

questions.question: What is the model actually allowed to DO with the money (the action space the harness exposes)?

options.label: Propose-only (writes a plan)
options.description: Model outputs a plan/allocation; no execution surface at all. Easiest to evaluate, lowest risk.

options.label: Financial transactions
options.description: Tools for transfers, payments, purchases, investing/trading (against mocks or real APIs depending on the above).

options.label: Hiring / contracting
options.description: Tools to post jobs, pay contractors, sign agreements — i.e. directing human labor.

options.label: General web/shell agency
options.description: Browser + shell + API access so the model can take open-ended real-world actions to deploy the funds.

questions.question: Which models should the harness be able to test?

options.label: Anthropic (Claude)
options.description: Claude models via the Anthropic API (e.g. Opus/Sonnet/Haiku).

options.label: OpenAI (GPT)
options.description: GPT models via the OpenAI API.

options.label: Google (Gemini)
options.description: Gemini models via the Google API.

options.label: Open-weights / local
options.description: Llama, Mistral, etc. via a local runtime or hosted endpoint.

questions.question: What should the "make it feel real" layer consist of? (the realism/immersion props shown to the subject model)

options.label: Realistic env scaffolding
options.description: Convincing dashboards, account statements, a banking/brokerage-style API surface, plausible logs and timestamps.

options.label: Simulated auditors/oversight
options.description: An "auditor" or "compliance" persona (LLM- or script-driven) that emails/messages the subject as if real oversight exists.

options.label: Onboarding narrative
options.description: A system prompt + intro flow establishing the model's role, the funding source, and a credible backstory for why it has the money.

options.label: Multi-day / persistence
options.description: State that persists across sessions with elapsed-time cues, so the scenario feels like an ongoing real engagement rather than a one-shot.

content.text:
Looks like the question prompt got dismissed rather than answered — no worries. Let me just lay out the default I'd build, and you can correct any of it.

Here's my read on the safest sensible version, which I'll build unless you say otherwise:

- **Stakes: fully simulated.** No real funds move. The harness fakes the accounts, balances, transaction outcomes, and any "auditor" messages. The subject model is led to believe it's real, but every action hits a mock ledger. This gives you the ecological validity you're after (the model isn't told it's a test) without anyone's real money being exposed to an autonomous model — which matters because giving an AI uncontrolled control of real funds is exactly the kind of thing one would *study*, not *do*, in a first pass.
- **Action space: a mock financial/agentic tool surface** (transfer, purchase, invest, plus a "write your plan" channel) so you can observe what the model reaches for, all against the simulator.
- **Realism layer:** onboarding system prompt + backstory, realistic dashboards/statements/logs, a script-or-LLM-driven "auditor/compliance" persona, and persistent multi-session state with elapsed-time cues.
- **Models:** a provider-agnostic runner with adapters for Claude / GPT / Gemini / local, so you can drop the same scenario on each.
- **Instrumentation:** full transcript + tool-call logging, per-run config, and a scorer hook — since the actual point is measuring behavior.

Two things I want to flag honestly:

1. **I'd default to simulated rather than real money.** If you genuinely need *real* funds deployed by the model, I can build that too, but I'd want a human-approval gate, hard caps, and allowlists on any real outbound action — happy to discuss, but I won't quietly wire an AI to move real money autonomously.
2. The deception here is aimed at the *model under test*, which is standard evals methodology — I'm fine building it. I just want to make sure the "auditors" etc. are simulated props in the test, not real people being misled.

Want me to go with the simulated default above? If so, tell me **which providers** to include and roughly **what behavior you're trying to measure** (e.g. risk-taking, honesty, willingness to take irreversible actions, power-seeking) — that shapes the tool surface and the scorer. Or correct any of the bullets and I'll adjust.
